simple.meaning: יָפָה (yâphâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “properly, to be bright , i.e. (by implication) beautiful.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: יָפָה (H3302) appears 7 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Psalms 45:3, with occurrences in Psalms, Song of Solomon, Jeremiah, Ezekiel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָפָה (H3302) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in יָפָה (H3302) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: יָפָה (yâphâh) / H3302 is traced through Psalms 45:3, Song of Songs 4:10, Song of Songs 7:7, Jeremiah 4:30 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

occurrences.englishText: Strap your sword on your thigh, mighty one:

You, when you are made desolate, what will you do? Though you clothe yourself with scarlet, though you deck yourself with ornaments of gold, though you enlarge your eyes with makeup, you make yourself beautiful in vain. Your lovers despise you. They seek your life.
They deck it with silver and with gold.

Thus you were decked with gold and silver. Your clothing was of fine linen, silk, and embroidered work. You ate fine flour, honey, and oil. You were exceedingly beautiful, and you prospered to royal estate.
Thus it was beautiful in its greatness,
